headline: Thani bin Abdullah Foundation, QU sign cooperation agreement
snippet:
Doha, Qatar: Qatar University (QU) signs a cooperation agreement with Thani bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services to enhance student support and strengthen collaboration in training, community engagement, and volunteer initiatives.

The agreement was signed by Vice President for Student Affairs at QU, Dr. Mohammad Diab, and  CEO of the Thani Bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services, Dr. Ayed bin Dabsan Al-Qahtani, in the presence of officials from both parties.

The agreement establishes an institutional framework for cooperation in providing financial assistance to QU students, implementing community service and awareness programmes, and organising conferences, workshops, and training courses aimed at developing skills and building capacity.

Commenting on the agreement, Vice President for Student Affairs at QU, Dr. Mohammad Diab, said, “This agreement reflects QU’s commitment to strengthening student support, developing students’ skills, and expanding opportunities for their active participation in community service, while fostering a stronger sense of social responsibility.”

For his part, CEO of the Thani Bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services, Dr. Ayed bin Dabsan Al-Qahtani, said, “This agreement reaffirms Thani Humanitarian Foundation’s commitment to supporting our students and enhancing their educational and community engagement opportunities. It also reflects our strong belief in the importance of partnership and cooperation among national institutions in this field, helping students continue their educational journey and further develop their capabilities.”

Dr. Ayed Al-Qahtani added, “Through our cooperation with Qatar University, we are keen to expand the scope of our joint efforts to include providing financial support services to students, implementing training, capacity-building and awareness programmes, and promoting a culture of volunteerism and community service.”

He continued, “We believe that integration and collaboration among educational, humanitarian and community institutions contribute to creating sustainable impact and pave the way for further initiatives that serve students and strengthen their engagement in society. We look forward to this agreement providing an effective framework for advancing cooperation between the Foundation and Qatar University, particularly as the national university represents the largest community of higher education students in Qatar. This encourages us to further our efforts and contributions toward providing our students with an outstanding educational environment.”

headline: Sure silver for sepak takraw women’s doubles
snippet: NAGOYA, Japan – The Philippines is now assured of another silver medal – potentially a gold if stars align – as the courageous sepak takraw women’s doubles squad continued its wondrous campaign at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026. On another rainy Monday, Sept. 28, the women’s crew of Nelly Jay Salon, Jean Marie Sucalit and Abegail Sinogbuhan overwhelmed Laos, 15-12, 15-10, in their semis match at the Mizuho Park Athletic Gymnasium. It was a remarkable win for the sepak takraw team, whose two-game winning run in the preliminary round was cut short by South Korea, 1-2, earlier in the day. Since it was a no-bearing match, they took the loss positively. True enough, against Laotian bets, they were precise and entertaining, what with their acrobatic kicks and rock-hard defense. But the men’s squad of Jayson Huerte, Jom Rafael, Rey Asilum, Glindil Phori, and Ronsited Gabayeron was not lucky enough, falling to Malaysian in riveting semis, 15-10, 11-15, 7-15, to settle for the bronze. Still, it was enough for the sepak takraw squad to eclipse its two-bronze medal haul in the Hangzhou Games three years ago. In the finals, the Filipinas will face Vietnam, which defeated South Korea, 15-6, 15-13, in the other semis match. Despite the latest bronze, Team Philippines remained in 16th place with two golds, two silver and 10 bronze medals at 4 p.m., with China enjoying the view atop the medal standings with 126 golds followed by Japan (39) and South Korea (21). For sure, there will be more good news to come heading to the final five days of this sporting spectacle among 45 countries. Tennis phenom Alex Eala is still playing against a Thai opponent as off press time, but she is expected to march into the next round, owing to her stellar resume. Olympians Nesthy Petecio and Carlo Paalam were scheduled to fight late Monday afternoon, with both boxers eyeing a semis berth that will guarantee a bronze medal each. However, they will be fighting against equally dangerous Chinese opponents. After two bronze medal finishes, PH officials and its adoring fans back home hope to finally win the ultimate prize in an esports event as Sibol’s Mobile Legends: Bang Bang squad begins its highly anticipated campaign at the Aichi Sky Expo in Japan on Tuesday, Sept. 29. Sibol earlier lost to China in the semifinals of the Honor of Kings event, which was expected anyway given China’s immense status. Despite the pressure as high as Mount Fuji, the Sibol squad is heavily favored to claim the gold medal in the Land of the Rising Sun starting with their game against Jordan in Group C at 2 p.m. and Kazakhstan at 5 p.m. on Tuesday. Well, they are not world champions in Mobile Legends for nothing. “There’s always going to be pressure, especially when people have high expectations of you. Being on top has all these expectations. We just have to stay grounded in our values and focus on our daily progress,” said Sibol coach Allec Alvarado. Karl “KarlTzy” Nepomuceno, inarguably the greatest Mobile Legends player of all time, is expected to lead the charge, along with Sanford “Sanford” Vinuya, Alston “Sanji” Pabico, Dave “Teddy” Viana, and Jaypee “Jaypee” Gonzales, and Duane “Kelra” Pillas. In tennis, Stefi Aludo and Tennielle Madis advanced to the second round of women’s doubles after a gutsy win over Indonesian rivals, while Patrick Coo finished seventh in the finals of the Cycling BMX Racing.
